public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The verified sources show a proposed IPO and an assessment of market warning signs, not a decisive industry-wide collapse. Neither continuing activity nor financial strain settles an assertion of inevitable eventual failure. No event found meets the early-resolution rule, so the forecast remains open.
limitations: Fall and the industry's boundaries are not precisely defined.
An IPO filing does not establish a successful offering or financial sustainability.
The available contextual reporting is not a complete industry dataset.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI industry will inevitably fall; its supporters have only delayed it.

statement.excerpt: The people that have so aggressively worked together to hold up this industry have only delayed its inevitable fall.

our_interpretation: In context, this industry means the commercial generative-AI industry and the infrastructure businesses supporting it.
The ordinary reading of fall is a broad commercial collapse, reflected in widespread business failures and sustained contraction in investment and commercial activity.
A stock-market decline, one company's failure or continued losses alone would not establish an industry-wide collapse.
No deadline is supplied. The nearby 2030 discussion concerns compute expansion and is not imported as a deadline for collapse.
Only delayed adds a causal assertion about supporters that would require separate evidence even if a collapse occurred.
criteria.support_condition: A broad collapse of the commercial generative-AI industry occurs, with widespread failures and sustained contraction across investment and commercial activity. Full support for the delay assertion additionally requires evidence that supporters prolonged the industry's survival.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive change makes the specified industry-collapse outcome impossible. Continued operation or expansion for a finite period cannot disprove an undated claim of eventual collapse.
